newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow drubbing sees Australian stocks dumped at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow drubbing sees Australian stocks dumped at open.

text.p: The Australian share market quickly headed south at the opening on Friday after Wall Street was walloped by ever-increasing fears of an interest rate hike at the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting on March 25.
The All Ordinaries index slumped 31.5 points to 2,421.1.
Losses were across the board, with both the industrials and resources sector losing ground and leaving local blue chips looking decidely weak in early trade.
"It was always going to be a matter of how far," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage, noting the breadth of the day's decline.
"It's across the board, much as you would expect."
Bellwether BHP paid for its leading role, dipping 1.6 percent to an intraday low of A$16.77 (US$13.25) before finding support.
This compared to the broader market's early loss of 1.3 percent. U.S.-leveraged media giant News Corp, headed the industrial losers, losing 1.9 percent to A$6.65.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of more than 10 to one, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
